field: *** PROVENANCE ***
value: KURT'S OWN PAPERS, PHOTOGRAPHED FROM THE FAMILY'S KEEPING AND SUPPLIED BY DERRICK ON 1 OCTOBER 2026. Two documents: a GERMAN DRIVING LICENCE with its INTERNATIONAL DRIVING PERMIT, Berlin 1934, and a GERMAN PASSPORT issued at the German Consulate in Johannesburg in 1939. Graded as what they are — originals held by the family, read at the image, not supplied by an archive.

field: DOC 1 — THE FÜHRERSCHEIN
value: Ausgestellt für Herrn KURT LUWINSKI, geboren am 11. 5. 1912 zu BERLIN, wohnhaft in BLN.-SCHÖNEBERG, MERANER-Straße Nr. 2. Form "Nr. 23 II (Berlin 1933), Preußische Druckerei- und Verlags-A.-G. Berlin".

field: the authorisation
value: Herr LUWINSKI ist ermächtigt, ein Kraftfahrzeug mit Antrieb durch VERBRENNUNGSMASCHINEN [Elektromotoren and Dampfmaschinen struck out] der Klasse — 3 — zu führen. BERLIN, den 30. JANUAR 1934. Signed for Der Polizeipräsident, stamped Abteilung III Kraftverkehrsamt, with two 2-Reichsmark Prussian administrative-fee stamps.

field: *** AND THAT DATE CONTRADICTS THE FAMILY TREE ***
value: THE TREE SAYS KURT EMIGRATED IN 1933 — "Johannesburg, Süd Afrika, 1933" — and this archive has published that year on four pages. ON 30 JANUARY 1934 HE WAS IN BERLIN, LIVING AT MERANER STRASSE 2, APPLYING TO THE BERLIN POLICE FOR A DRIVING LICENCE AND PAYING FOUR MARKS FOR IT. Either the year in the tree is wrong, or he left and came back. THE DOCUMENT CANNOT TELL WHICH and this archive is not choosing: what it can say is that A MAN WHO HAD EMIGRATED IN 1933 DID NOT TAKE OUT A BERLIN DRIVING LICENCE FROM A SCHÖNEBERG ADDRESS IN JANUARY 1934, so the plain year is no longer safe.

field: and the date has a second face, which is not an argument
value: 30 JANUARY 1934 IS THE FIRST ANNIVERSARY OF HITLER'S APPOINTMENT AS CHANCELLOR. The coincidence is recorded because it is a fact about the date. It means nothing about the man and is not offered as though it did.

field: DOC 2 — THE INTERNATIONAL DRIVING PERMIT
value: DEUTSCHES REICH · Internationaler Kraftfahrzeugverkehr · INTERNATIONALER FÜHRERSCHEIN · Internationales Abkommen vom 24. April 1926. Ausstellung des Scheins — Ort: BERLIN. Tag: 26 [MONTH ILLEGIBLE] 193[4]. Der Polizeipräsident, Abt. III Kraftverkehrsamt, with the Berlin police stamp. Form "A 82, Reichsdruckerei, Berlin (10.31)".

field: what is and is not readable on it
value: THE DAY IS 26 AND THE PLACE IS BERLIN. The month is a faded rubber stamp and IS NOT READ HERE; the year is taken as 1934 because an international permit under the 1926 Convention is issued against an existing domestic licence, and the domestic licence is dated 30 January 1934. SO THE PERMIT IS ON OR AFTER THAT DAY and the archive is not inventing a month to make a better sentence.

field: *** WHY AN INTERNATIONAL PERMIT MATTERS MORE THAN A DRIVING LICENCE ***
value: AN INTERNATIONALER FÜHRERSCHEIN IS A DOCUMENT FOR DRIVING OUTSIDE GERMANY. A man takes one out because he expects to be abroad. Taken with the domestic licence weeks earlier, the pair reads as preparation rather than routine — AND THAT IS A READING, NOT A FINDING. He may simply have wanted to drive on holiday.

field: and its identity page is blank
value: page 3, "Angaben über den Führer", carries his photograph and the Berlin police stamp, and the five numbered fields — Name, Vorname, Ort der Geburt, Tag der Geburt, Wohnort — ARE EMPTY, struck through with a single looping pen stroke. The particulars were never entered. The booklet was issued, stamped, photographed and left incomplete.

field: *** MERANER STRASSE 2, AND IT IS FOUR YEARS EARLIER THAN THE ARCHIVE HAD IT ***
value: the 1939 census puts JACOB, AUGUSTE AND SIEGFRIED at MERANER STRASSE 2, and the 1939 Adressbuch has "LEIBHOLZ, J., KFM." in that house. THE LICENCE PUTS KURT AT THE SAME ADDRESS IN JANUARY 1934. The family's tenancy of that flat now begins at least five years earlier than any document previously showed, and Kurt was living in it.

field: DOC 3 — THE REISEPASS, PERSONENBESCHREIBUNG
value: Beruf: HUTMACHER. Geburtsort: Berlin. Geburtstag: 11.5.1912. Wohnort: JOHANNESBURG (rubber-stamped in blue). Gestalt: mittel. Gesicht: oval. Farbe der Augen: braun. Farbe des Haares: braun. Besondere Kennzeichen: — . The EHEFRAU column and the whole KINDER table are struck through with a diagonal line.

field: *** HUTMACHER FILLS THE HOLE IN THE TRADE ***
value: this archive already held the chain and could not close it: AUGUSTE was a Schneiderin und Modistin — a dressmaker and MILLINER; SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ sold "HÜTE EN GROS" — wholesale hats — at Kommandantenstraße 29; and KURT BOUGHT THE PICCADILLY HAT COMPANY at 81 Eloff Street in November 1941. But Kurt's own stated trade was "dress designer" in 1933 and again in 1956, and the hats looked like something he took up in Johannesburg. HERE IS HIS OWN WORD FOR IT IN 1939, TWO YEARS BEFORE HE BOUGHT THE SHOP: HUTMACHER. HE WAS A HATTER BEFORE HE OWNED A HAT SHOP.

field: and the struck-out columns are evidence too
value: no wife, no children, July 1939. The 1948 Johannesburg marriage register calls him a BACHELOR at thirty-six, and this agrees with it nine years earlier.

field: DOC 4 — THE SIGNATURE PAGE
value: photograph, Lichtbild, over the stamp "DEUTSCHES KONSULAT IN JOHANNESBURG" with eagle and swastika. "Unterschrift des Paßinhabers:" — and in his own hand, *** ISRAEL KURT LUWINSKI ***. The printed words "und seiner Ehefrau" are struck out. "Es wird hiermit bescheinigt, daß der Inhaber die durch das obenstehende Lichtbild dargestellte Person ist und die darunter befindliche Unterschrift eigenhändig vollzogen hat. JOHANNESBURG, den 26. JULI 1939."

field: *** WHICH ANSWERS THE OPEN QUESTION ON HIS PAGE ***
value: Kurt's page has asked for weeks WHERE "ISRAEL" COMES FROM, noting that as the son of a Jewish father and a Catholic mother he would ordinarily have been Mischling ersten Grades, to whom the 1938 name decree did not apply. THE ANSWER IS THAT A GERMAN CONSULATE APPLIED IT TO HIM ANYWAY, SIX THOUSAND MILES AWAY, AND HE SIGNED IT HIMSELF. It is not a family-tree embellishment and it is not something he carried out of Germany in 1933 — the decree is of 17 August 1938, five years after he left.

field: and what it does NOT answer
value: WHY the consulate treated him as a Jew rather than as a Mischling. The document records the classification and gives no reason for it. The question is not closed; IT IS SHARPER, because it is now a question about an act by a named office on a known day rather than about a word on a family tree.

field: DOC 5 — GELTUNGSBEREICH
value: In- und Ausland — valid at home and abroad. "Der Paß wird ungültig am 25. JULI 1940, wenn er nicht verlängert wird." Ausstellende Behörde: DEUTSCHES KONSULAT JOHANNESBURG. Datum: 26. JULI 1939. ONE YEAR'S VALIDITY, and the war began five weeks into it.

field: DOC 6 — A SOUTH AFRICAN ENDORSEMENT
value: an oval purple stamp reading IMMIGRATION OFFICER · SOUTH AFRICA, with "PASSED" and "INITIALS", dated 8 [MONTH ILLEGIBLE] 1939 and initialled. He presented the new German passport to South African immigration within about six weeks of its issue. The month is overwritten by the officer's initials and IS NOT READ HERE.

field: *** AND THE THING THAT IS NOT A FACT AT ALL ***
value: THREE PHOTOGRAPHS OF KURT, two from the 1934 licence booklets and one from the 1939 passport. A young man of twenty-one in profile, smiling; the same man three-quarter face in sepia; and a man of twenty-seven at a consular counter. This archive has written about him for weeks from register numbers and gazette notices. DERRICK HAS HAD HIS FACE ALL ALONG.
